SWEEP 5 — GPU-sharing / fleet-fit (verified live 2026-08-01)

## 1. Pack density: what fits N-up on one H100 80GB

Verified live: Qwen configs fetched from HF raw config.json today (2026-08-01); gpt-oss size from live cheat-sheet. Weight sizes at Q4_K_M (~0.57 B/param) and Q8_0 (~1.06 B/param) are computed from verified param counts — marked (calc). KV/token computed from fetched configs (hybrid models pay KV only on full-attention layers).

| Model | Arch (verified) | Q4 wts | Q8 wts | KV @32k ctx/session | Replicas/H100 @Q8 (+~6GB KV ea) | @Q4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B | dense hybrid, 32L, 8 full-attn, 4 KV-heads×256 (config fetched 8/1) | ~5.4GB (calc) | ~10GB (calc) | 32KiB/tok → 1.0GB | **4x** | 6x |
| Gemma-4 12B | dense (vLLM docs 6/3/26) | ~6.9GB (calc) | ~12.8GB (calc) | est (config not fetched) | **4x** | 5-6x |
| gpt-oss-20b | MoE, native MXFP4 ~14GB on disk (computingforgeeks, ~1wk old) | n/a (ships MXFP4) | — | small (SWA) | **4x** (MXFP4) | — |
| Qwen3.6-27B | dense hybrid GDN, 64L, 16 full-attn, 4 KV-heads×256 (config fetched 8/1) | ~15.5GB (calc) | ~28.8GB (calc) | 64KiB/tok → 2.0GB | **2x** ← the proven pair regime | 4x |
| Gemma-4 26B-A4B | MoE (official) | ~15GB (calc) | ~28GB (calc) | est | **2x** | 4x |
| Gemma-4 31B | dense | ~17.8GB (calc) | ~33GB (calc) | est | **2x** | 3x |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | MoE 256 experts/8 active, 40L, 10 full-attn, 2 KV-heads×256 (config fetched 8/1) | ~20GB (calc) | ~37GB (calc) | 20KiB/tok → 0.64GB | **2x** (tight) | 3x |

Generalization of the +60% pair result: every memra 20-40B model at Q8 lands exactly in the proven ~32GB/replica regime → pair-packing should transfer fleet-wide as-is. The 4-15B class opens an **unproven 4-6x regime** — the mechanism (per-replica SM/bandwidth undersubscription at low batch) predicts continued gains until aggregate HBM bandwidth saturates, but 4x needs on-box measurement before claiming it. Bonus: Qwen hybrid-GDN KV is tiny (8-16 of 32-64 layers pay KV), so KV budget barely constrains pack count — dense-full-attention competitors can't pack this densely at long context.

## 2. Multi-model co-residency / cascade demand

- Commercial routing/cascade layer is real and crowded (all verified live): **Not Diamond** (learned meta-router over 60+ models, github.com/Not-Diamond/awesome-ai-model-routing), **Martian** (dynamic per-request routing), **Morph Router** ($0.001/classification, ~430ms, morphllm.com 6/15/26), **OpenRouter** routing, **vLLM Semantic Router** (OSS, released Jan 2026 — zylos.ai research 1/29/26), LiteLLM; 2026 trend per Zylos (3/2/26): bandit-feedback online routers + MCP gateways as control planes.
- What NOBODY found is doing commercially: **routing tiers co-resident on one GPU**. All routers route across API endpoints. darklanes' pack-proven 9B+27B co-residency (10+29GB Q8 = 39GB, fits with full KV budgets) would serve a triage->answer cascade with zero network hop and shared admission — an open niche, not a copied feature.
- Note: draft/target co-residency is already solved *inside* the model for this fleet via MTP (Gemma 4 drafters literally share the target's KV cache — Google blog 5/5/26), so the cascade value is in *quality* tiering, not spec decoding.

Economics: **100% of memra's current 7-model fleet is spec-capable with first-party heads/drafters** — the measured 1.35-1.76x MTP multiplier applies fleet-wide, and it compounds multiplicatively with pack density (2 replicas × 1.5x spec ≈ 3x tok/s/GPU vs naive single-replica non-spec). Gemma 4's official 3x claim (and vendor note of ~2.2x on 26B-A4B at batch 4-8) says memra's 1.35-1.76 has verified headroom, not a ceiling.

## 4. KV-reuse / session-affinity — what cached tokens sell for (live prices)

| Provider | Base input /1M | Cached read /1M | Discount | Source (date) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Anthropic (Sonnet 4.6) | $3.00 | $0.30 (writes 1.25x 5-min / 2x 1-hr) | 90% | platform.claude.com/docs pricing (crawled ~7/31/26) |
| OpenAI (GPT-5.5) | $5.00 | $0.50 | 90% | finout.io 7/26; live table at developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (2 days old) |
| OpenAI (GPT-5.4) | $2.50 | ~$0.25 | 90% | morphllm.com 6/18/26 |
| DeepSeek V4-Flash | $0.14 (miss) | **$0.0028 (hit)** | **98%** | api-docs.deepseek.com (15h old) + chat-deep.ai 7/29/26 |
| DeepSeek V4-Pro | $0.435 | $0.003625 | ~99% | benchlm.ai (1wk old) |
| Google Gemini 3.1 Pro | $2.00 | $0.20 explicit; implicit caching default-on for 2.5+ | 90% | ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/caching (~4wks old) |

Read: the market has converged on 90-98% discounts for cache hits — i.e., providers price a KV-hit token at 2-10% of a fresh one, and Anthropic charges a 25-100% *premium* to write cache, confirming memory residency is the scarce resource. Use-cases that reward memra's KV-prefix-reuse: agent loops (every tool-call turn re-reads the same growing prefix — the dominant traffic shape in 2026 routing writeups), long chats with session affinity, fixed-system-prompt/RAG-corpus serving. DeepSeek's 98% figure is the strongest signal that a cache-hit token costs the operator almost nothing — every prefix memra reuses is nearly pure margin, and the spill stack (KV to 2TB RAM / 28TB NVMe on H100 boxes) extends the "1-hour TTL" product dimension far past what HBM-only competitors hold.

## Bottom line
1. Pair-packing transfers directly: the whole 20-40B fleet at Q8 sits at the proven ~32GB/replica point; 4-15B at Q8 opens an unmeasured 4x regime (measure before claiming).
2. Cascade routing is a hot commercial layer (Not Diamond, Martian, Morph, OpenRouter, vLLM Semantic Router) but all of it routes across endpoints — single-GPU co-resident tiering (9B triage + 27B answer, 39GB Q8) is an open niche darklanes can occupy today.
3. Spec heads are now table stakes on exactly memra's fleet: Qwen3.5/3.6 ship native MTP in config, Gemma 4 shipped official Apache-2.0 MTP drafters (5/5/26) claiming up to 3x — the 1.35-1.76x strength applies to 7/7 models and has documented headroom.
4. Cached-token pricing (90-98% discounts industry-wide) is the direct revenue comp for KV reuse; DeepSeek's $0.0028/1M cache-hit rate is the margin ceiling signal.

Caveats: Q4/Q8 GB figures marked (calc) are computed from verified param counts, not weighed GGUF files; Gemma-4 per-config KV not fetched; gpt-oss-20b MTP absence and 4x-pack throughput gains are unverified.

## Trend read (May-Jul 2026)

1. **Openness and runnability split into two axes.** Four trillion-class open drops in four months (V4-Pro 1.6T Apr, M3 428B Jun, GLM-5.2 744B Jun, K3 2.8T Jul; Qwen3.8 2.4T promised). All MIT/near-MIT, all 1M-context, none loadable outside a server room. The consumer tier hasn't moved since April (Qwen3.6) except Gemma 4 12B.
2. **MTP heads went mainstream.** Qwen3.5/3.6 train MTP into the trunk, GLM-5.2 ships an improved MTP/NextN layer, llama.cpp merged draft-mtp support (PR #22673), and MTP-bundled GGUFs are a norm. Directly plays to memra's speculative strength.
3. **Total-vs-active spread exploded**: 13B-104B active on 284B-2800B totals; routed-expert residency (not full-weight residency) is now the defining serving problem — exactly darklanes' spill-stack thesis. GLM-5.2 (744B/40B, MIT, MTP) and V4-Flash-0731 (284B/13B, MIT, llama.cpp-supported) are the most spill-servable high-value targets.
4. **Native low-bit is here**: K3's MXFP4 weights are QAT-native from SFT onward; NVIDIA publishes NVFP4 checkpoints (M3).
5. **Attention is hybridizing everywhere**: GDN (Qwen), KDA (K3), MSA (M3), DSA+IndexShare (GLM) — every frontier open model now needs custom-attention engine support; plain GQA no longer sufficient.
6. **China leads open, and may retrench**: Qwen went Max-first/closed for 3.7 and 3.8; Reuters 07-07 reported MOFCOM talks with Alibaba/ByteDance/Z.ai about restricting overseas access to advanced open weights (consultation stage only). US side: Gemma 4's Apache-2.0 day-one drop is the counterexample; Meta and OpenAI open lines are static (Apr/Aug 2025).
7. **Benchmark battleground is agentic coding**: SWE-bench Pro/Verified, Terminal Bench 2.1, long-horizon agent suites dominate every release post.

### 4. Where darklanes' capabilities map to margin

**a) Kimi K3 spill — the flagship case.** 1.4TB MXFP4 fits *entirely in the 2TB RAM* of an H100 box (no NVMe fault path needed; RAM→HBM over PCIe, exactly the tuned spill stack). Conventional hosts need ≥2 full H100 nodes or B200/GB300 ($41.5–80+/hr). At $14/M out, a 1–2-GPU spill box ($5–10/hr) breaks even at **~100–200 tok/s aggregate** — every 100 tok/s = $5.04/hr revenue. Gap from today: ~20–40x (vs 500–2,000x at DeepSeek-class prices). Caveat: 104B active ≈ 52GB/token cold at FP4; PCIe gen5 (~64GB/s) bounds cold-expert single-stream at ~1 tok/s — the margin depends on SLRU residency hit-rate + cross-batch expert sharing, which is precisely the multi-user-spill measurement not yet taken. K2.5 (1T/32B-active, ~550GB) is the easier warm-up: fits RAM trivially, 16GB/token cold, but only $2.25/M — break-even ~330 tok/s/GPU.

**b) Exactness premium — verified nobody sells it.** Checked live: vLLM batch-invariance is a self-host flag with documented hardware dependence; SGLang's deterministic mode (built on Thinking Machines' batch-invariant ops, Sept 2025) is likewise a feature with a throughput tax, not a provider SLA (thinkingmachines.ai; cloudai.pt Jul 2026; arXiv 2511.17826). No API provider offers bit-reproducible outputs as a product. memra's exactness is architectural *and* throughput-positive (speculative/graph token-identical). A "reproducible endpoint" SLA at 2–3x floor flips class-1/2 math: 9B at $0.45/M → break-even ~990–1,730 tok/s/GPU on cheap hosts, roughly where the +67% increment lands. Buyers: eval labs, RL training loops, LLM-as-judge, regulated, agent debugging.

**c) Latency premium is proven demand.** In the same live endpoints pull, Groq sells llama-3.3-70b at $0.79 out vs DeepInfra's $0.32 — 2.5x for speed, and gets ranked traffic. memra's decode wins (7/7 vs vLLM) and MTP (1.35–1.76x) are a single-stream product: premium fast endpoints on the 27B/35B class, priced Groq-style, need far fewer tok/s/GPU to clear cost.

**d) Batch/async is a cost lever, not a moat.** DeepInfra flex tier = 0.8x base (live 2026-08-01; priority = 1.5x). Batch-only serving on interruptible marketplace GPUs ($0.90–1.60) improves the denominator ~3x vs a capacity block — worth doing, but only multiplies whichever of (a)–(c) you already win.

**e) Dedicated instance-hours dodge per-token competition entirely.** "Private Kimi-K2.5/K3 endpoint on 1–2 GPUs" at $6–10/hr vs the $25–80/hr a conventional deployment costs the customer — margin on the capability itself, no tok/s break-even required. This is sellable at *today's* single-digit tok/s for latency-tolerant private/batch users.

**Bottom line ranking by margin proximity:** (1) 30–40B multi-user at floor/premium — needs task #35 to land ~300–800 tok/s/GPU aggregate; (2) exactness-SLA premium on anything served; (3) K3/K2.5 spill — target 100–200 tok/s aggregate on 1–2 GPUs at $14/M, or sell as dedicated instance-hours now; (4) 7–15B commodity — only viable inside (2)/(d); (5) DeepSeek-class and 70B dense at commodity prices — structurally out.

**2TB RAM verdict: every bank fits.** Even K3's 1,446 GB fits with ~400 GB headroom (NVMe = load staging + cold tier only, not the hot path — a first for this class). Everything else fits 2-9x over, leaving RAM for pinned rings and page cache.

**HBM budget (trunk must be resident):** GLM-5.2/K2.7/M3/Qwen3.5/Flash trunks are 8-21 GB at Q6 → **45-60 GB of HBM left as SLRU expert cache** (11-25% of bank resident → h=75-90% is realistic given adjacent-token expert overlap; memra's own Hy3 SLRU data supports this). Kimi K3 trunk needs Q4-class (~43 GB) → only ~15-20 GB cache (1.4% of bank) → K3 single-stream lands 3-6 tok/s, PCIe-bound. DSv4-Pro is the worst fit: 129B trunk ≈ 72 GB even at Q4.5 — fits on paper with near-zero expert cache; hardest candidate despite mid-size bank.

**Two structural advantages nobody's numbers above capture:**
- **Prefill.** CPU-offload rigs collapse at ~1-20 tok/s prefill (the documented killer). Spill prefill fetches each expert once per chunk and applies it to all chunk tokens on-GPU: GLM-5.2 = 408 GB/55 GB/s ≈ 7.4 s per 2K-token chunk ≈ **~275 tok/s prefill floor**; even K3 ≈ 78 tok/s — 50-80x the homelab pattern.
- **Batch amortization (darklanes angle).** Concurrent sequences share fetched experts; aggregate tok/s scales far better than single-stream, which is exactly the multi-user product.
- **MTP:** GLM-5.2 ships an improved MTP layer (+20% acceptance, per model card); MiniMax M3 ships **seven** MTP modules; K2.7/DSv4 have 1 each. memra's MTP speculative strength (1.35-1.76x) multiplies directly onto the h=75% numbers.

# SYNTHESIS — Most valuable OSS model for darklanes (2026-08-01)

## 1. THE ANSWER: Hy3 (Tencent Hunyuan 3) now, GLM-5.2 as the strategic build, K3 as dedicated-instance flagship only

**Primary: serve the full public Hy3 on single H100s via the spill stack.** The argument, in order of the evidence:

**Demand.** Hy3 is the #3 model on the planet by OpenRouter weekly tokens (4.8T), growing +73%/wk — the fastest grower in the top 10 — and it has exactly **5 endpoints worldwide** (re-verified by me today via the OpenRouter API). DeepSeek V4 Flash, by contrast, has 22 endpoints all pinned at first-party price with undercutters below — zero margin. Hy3 is the single clearest demand/supply gap on the board, and it is the only such gap where memra has zero architecture bring-up cost.

**What memra uniquely brings.** The architecture is already in-tree — the spill stack was literally tuned on Hy3 (5090, REAP50 overlay, ~5 tok/s single-stream today). On an H100 the regime flips from hostile to friendly: the ~157 GB Q4-class full bank vs 80 GB HBM means roughly half the expert bank sits resident next to a ~21B-active trunk, versus 6.5x-over-VRAM on the 24GB card. Nobody else has a single-GPU big-MoE path with real prefill (the chunked-expert prefill pattern gives a transfer-bound floor in the hundreds of tok/s where KTransformers-style CPU offload collapses to 1-20). Second unique lever: 3 of Hy3's 5 endpoints are fp8 and one is quant-"unknown" — the exact provider-fidelity complaint documented in the LessWrong pinning post and OpenRouter's own blog. memra's exactness (spec/graph token-identical) plus a pinned, disclosed quantization is a sellable SLA no Hy3 provider offers.

**Engineering distance.** Smallest of any candidate: port the spill stack to the H100 box, build a full-bank (un-pruned) serving artifact from the pinned BF16 source, run the existing gate battery. No new attention family, no new tokenizer, no new router. Honest caveat: what memra serves *today* is the REAP50-pruned research overlay — that is not sellable as "Hy3." Full-bank artifact + quality gates is the real deliverable, and it is days-to-low-weeks of work, not a bring-up.

**Revenue math.** At the market price ($0.528/M out, $0.132/M in), a $2.69/hr RunPod H100 breaks even at ~1,415 tok/s output-only, or **~700 tok/s aggregate assuming a typical 4:1 input mix**; a $1.60 marketplace host needs ~420. That is aggressive but the right order: memra already measured 493 tok/s/GPU aggregate on a 9B, and Hy3-on-H100 is a mostly-HBM-resident 21B-active MoE with batch-shared expert fetches — the cross-batch measurement (not yet taken) decides it. If aggregate lands below break-even, the fallback is not failure: premium tiers (Hy3's endpoints already span $0.528-$0.80 out), full-262K-ctx serving (scarce industry-wide), the exactness SLA at 2-3x floor, or listing as OpenRouter's 6th Hy3 provider into a +73%/wk demand curve.

**Secondary (start now, lands later): GLM-5.2.** It is where the *money* is — agents + code are ~56% of OpenRouter spend, and GLM-5.2 is the OSS spearhead (#3 in both Code Generation and Workflow Execution spend, rising; the $18-160/mo GLM Coding Plan proves subscription demand). MIT, 1M ctx, ships an improved MTP head that multiplies directly onto memra's proven 1.35-1.76x speculative strength. Spill math is friendly (408 GB bank, ~25B trunk, ~275 tok/s prefill floor, 10-25 tok/s single-stream *ceiling from geometry — not measured*). Cost: a real bring-up (DSA sparse attention + IndexShare + MLA-style trunk = a new attention family), which is also the hedge — see §4. Note a report conflict: Report 2 calls GLM-5.2 "#1 open on AA Index (51)" but Report 0's fresher data puts K3 at ~57 above it; do not print the #1 claim.

**Tertiary (demo/flagship, not token resale): Kimi K3** — see §3.

## 3. Spill-moat verdict: real edge, in two forms — demo in the third

**The demand side of the moat is confirmed:** margins collapse exactly where models run everywhere (V4 Flash, 22 endpoints) and hold exactly where weight class constrains supply (Hy3: #3 by volume, 5 endpoints; K3: $14-15/M pinned across all 10, zero undercutting). Supply-constrained big-MoE serving is the one segment on the board where a small provider can price.

**Form 1 (real, near):** Hy3-class — bank ≈ 2x HBM, mostly resident, batch-shared. This is a genuine business if the aggregate measurement clears ~400-700 tok/s.

**Form 2 (real, today, no tok/s bar):** dedicated private endpoints. "Your own K2.7/K3/GLM-5.2 on 1-2 H100s at $6-10/hr" versus the $25-80/hr a conventional deployment costs — the margin is on the capability, sellable at current single-digit tok/s to latency-tolerant private/batch buyers.

**Form 3 (demo until measured):** interactive token-resale of true giants (K3 at 3-6 tok/s single-stream). Every tok/s number in Report 2 is a transfer-bound ceiling from verified config geometry with *assumed* hit rates (h=75/90%) — the cross-batch expert-sharing hit rate, the single number the whole thesis pivots on, has never been measured. The structural prefill advantage (~78-275 tok/s floors vs CPU-offload collapse) is the strongest defensible claim; the decode economics are a hypothesis until the H100 run exists.

## 4. Trend hedge — what kills this in 3 months

- **Qwen3.8 open-weights drop (2.4T):** announced 07-19, API-only so far; Qwen 3.7 weights never shipped, so probability is low — but if it lands Apache 2.0 it reshuffles the frontier tier overnight.
- **MOFCOM export restriction** (Reuters 07-07, consultation stage): Hy3, GLM, K3 and successors are all Chinese. A restriction chokes *future* supply — which makes already-released weights **more** valuable and makes archiving them now the cheapest hedge in this document.
- **A "Hy3-Flash" or 6th-22nd Hy3 provider wave:** the 5-endpoint gap is the margin; it can close from either side. Recheck endpoint count before every pricing decision.
- **GLM-5.3 / DeepSeek V5 / a fresh Kimi:** cadence says one frontier open drop per month.

**The engineering hedge:** two attention families cover essentially every frontier open MoE. memra's existing GDN work is adjacent to KDA (K3) and Qwen hybrids; an **MLA-family trunk bring-up covers GLM-5.2, DeepSeek V4 Pro/Flash, and Kimi K2.x simultaneously**.
